target_customer: Developers and teams running AI agents that need many tool integrations
problem: Connecting agents to many tools means repeated sign ins and credential sprawl across clients; Executor offers one gateway for MCP, GraphQL and OpenAPI sources.
business_model: Open source core with hosted cloud plans, per member pricing reported by third parties
product_category: MCP gateway and agent tool integration layer

founders.name: Rhys Sullivan
previous_startups: Answer Overflow (bootstrapped, 1.5M monthly users per YC launch post)

competitors.name: Composio
competitors.what: Managed integrations and infrastructure for agent tools
competitors.traction_then: Widely cited as the main comparison to Executor in 2026 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Gateway across MCP, GraphQL and OpenAPI with per tool permissions and sandboxed execution is standard engineering with some hard parts, built by one founder.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and many rivals; stored credentials and connected accounts give mild switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many gateways launched in 2025 and 2026; no incumbent acquired or copied Executor in sources found.

market_need_then: MCP became a common agent integration standard and many gateway comparisons existed in 2026, pointing to demand for managing agent tool access.

identity.visual_style: Developer tool site with testimonials from X posts
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and setup focused, 'your agent does the thinking'

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repo with a Discord and thousands of GitHub stars (counts vary by source, about 1k to 4.5k)

brand_strength.rationale: Open source traction helps developer awareness, but the common word name is generic and shares search space with other tools named executor.

outcome_analysis: Executor is a solo founder Summer 2026 YC company with an open source MCP gateway that gained thousands of GitHub stars and appears in 2026 comparisons against Composio. No funding, exit or revenue is verified. The crowded gateway market and open source model make distribution the main question.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with no date or investors and no second source, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. GitHub star counts conflict across sources. Search for outcome events found nothing.
